task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper and terminal on the floor)
structural roles from usage crossed with residual structural influence
separability of coverage from talent and usage counts
methodological_questions: Does coverage vary enough within team-seasons, beyond what random assignment of player roles to stints would produce?
Is coverage separable from talent and counts, given that roles are defined from usage and a usage-residualized influence?
Does the talent control behave: not collinear with coverage, stable across seasons, not built from the same possessions as the roles?
How stable and reliable are player role labels (median splits, residual sign) across games and seasons?
Is there enough effective sample at the team-season level (90 units) for the between-team parts, given that the stint-level data is clustered?
evidence_establishes: No historical evidence was available: retrieve_history returned zero records, so no earlier study of this question, its status or its failures can be cited.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether role coverage has been measured before, whether coverage varies within team, whether it is separable from talent or counts, or whether any talent control has been tried and how it behaved. An empty retrieval says nothing about whether such work exists elsewhere.
own_inferences: The glossary defines roles by crossing usage (above or below the rotation median) with residual influence (influence beyond what usage predicts). Roles are therefore partly defined by counts, so 'separable from counts' is not automatic. The residual is orthogonal to usage by construction in the player-season fit. That orthogonality is mechanical and does not show separability at the lineup level.

Terminal Scorer and Primary Organizer are both high-usage categories. With a median split, about half of rotation players are high-usage, so the chance that a five-man unit lacks any high-usage player is small. Coverage of those two roles may be near-saturated and may mostly track total lineup usage or minutes. Shaper coverage probably carries most of the variation.

If roles are estimated on the same possessions or games used to describe lineup coverage or talent, any apparent separability or talent-control behavior can be circular. Roles, talent and coverage must be estimated on disjoint data.
The question has three parts and mostly asks for diagnostics rather than an outcome effect. It can be tested only if each part gets a pre-set numeric criterion.

90 team-seasons matches three full seasons (2022-23 to 2024-25). The 2025-26 data, listed as complete by 2026-04-13 for the regular season and 2026-06-21 for the playoffs, may be unused and could serve as a holdout.
uncertainties: The exact rule and reliability of role labels, including the rule for Connector and any role-assignment code. Only the Structural Influence paper definitions are given.
Which talent measure is available. The listed files are play-by-play, rotations, starters, matchup minutes and box-score summary, with no stated talent rating.
Whether 2025-26 data is included in the 90 units. [prior work] states 90 team-seasons, but the date lists four seasons.
Number of distinct stints or lineups per team-season, and minutes per lineup, which are not stated.
Whether roles are assigned per player-season, per half-season, or on rolling pre-game windows.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned no records, so no earlier findings or failed approaches could shape the decision. The decision rests only on the task statement, the glossary definitions and my own inference. The design is built from first principles and guards against circularity and mechanical coupling, which are risks I identified, not ones any record reported.

blocking_constraints.text: Roles are defined from usage and a usage-residualized influence, and coverage is a deterministic function of the roles of five players. Coverage can be close to a function of lineup usage and rotation composition. Without a null that preserves usage distributions, 'separable from counts' cannot be tested.

Role labels come from median splits and residual sign. Players near the threshold flip labels with sampling noise, which will create or hide coverage variation. If reliability is not shown to be adequate, the within-team variation claim cannot be interpreted.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so whether this has been answered is unknown. The glossary points to the Structural Influence paper and later studies using role labels, but no record of their results on coverage was returned, and none is described here.

risks.text: Coverage of Organizer and Terminal is nearly implied by lineup usage and the median split. Variation and 'separability' can be mechanical. Use a within-team permutation null that keeps each player's usage and minutes.

Roles, talent and coverage estimated from the same games or possessions make the talent control and the separability check circular. Estimate roles and talent on disjoint earlier data, such as the prior season or odd and even games, and evaluate coverage on later stints.

Residual influence and talent proxies built from points or PPP embed outcomes. If coverage is later linked to efficiency, the label already encodes the outcome. Keep outcomes out of the diagnostic stage.
Role labels are unstable near the usage median and the residual-zero line. Measure split-half label agreement and propagate it into coverage.

Coverage tracks which players are on the floor, which depends on talent, minutes, starters, injuries, foul trouble, score and garbage time. Talent control may absorb the roles themselves, since high-influence players tend to be high-talent.

Possessions (420,993) are heavily clustered. The effective n for between-team claims is 90 team-seasons, and lineup-level estimates are thin for rare lineups. Using possessions as independent units would overstate power.
Lineups missing a role may be rare and short-lived, so low-coverage cells can have too few minutes. Playoffs have fewer teams (16 per season), and rotations are tighter.
Roles and talent change within and across seasons through trades, injuries and the playoffs. Pooling seasons or using full-season labels for early stints can mislead.
Three coverage roles, three or more criteria, several talent proxies, and RS versus PO splits multiply comparisons unless the confirmatory set is fixed.
The play-type classifier and initiator attribution come from text-inferred play-by-play, so initiation counts, and hence usage and residual influence, carry classification error.
Stint reconstruction from substitution intervals and ten-player on-court tracking can misassign players. Validate against box-score minutes and starters.

design.estimand: Three pre-specified diagnostic quantities. (1) Within-team variation: the share of variance in stint-level (minutes-weighted) coverage for each role, and for all three together, that lies within team-season. This is compared with the same share under a permutation null that reshuffles role labels among rotation players within each team-season while preserving usage and minutes. (2) Separability: the share of coverage variance not explained by talent and counts (lineup mean usage, lineup minutes, number of high-usage players), and the partial association of coverage with a stint-level outcome-free descriptor. (3) Talent control behavior: collinearity with coverage, out-of-sample stability, and a sign and monotonicity check.
design.unit: Primary: the stint or lineup within team-season, weighted by possessions and clustered by team-season. Secondary: team-season (n=90) for between-team statements.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 (90 team-seasons) as the development sample. Exclude garbage time and lineups with fewer than a fixed minimum number of possessions, set before looking at data. Playoffs are analyzed separately and descriptively. Use the 2025-26 regular season as a confirmatory holdout only if it is outside the stated 90 units, with thresholds frozen before it is opened.
design.power: No formal power for a hypothesis about an outcome effect is claimed. The criteria are precision-based. Use a cluster bootstrap over team-seasons and report 95% intervals. The within-team variance share must be estimable with an interval half-width under 0.10. If more than a pre-set fraction of coverage cells (for example 20%) fall below the minimum-possession cutoff, report the part as underpowered and not as a null.
design.controls: Roles and talent are estimated only on data disjoint from the data used to measure coverage (prior season or alternating games). Talent proxies must not be built from the same possessions or from points. Candidates are prior-season minutes-weighted box-score value and prior-season on/off from earlier games. Control for lineup minutes, starter status, period, score margin (excluding garbage time), and team-season fixed effects. Report split-half role label agreement and re-run with a buffer zone around the median and residual zero (drop near-threshold players).
design.falsification: (a) Within-team permutation null of role labels with usage and minutes preserved. Coverage variation must exceed it. (b) Negative control: shuffle talent across team-seasons and confirm the talent coefficients vanish. (c) Placebo roles: assign roles from random splits of players with the same marginal rates and confirm the diagnostics do not hold. (d) Cross-season check: the talent control and separability results must hold in each season, not only pooled. (e) Label-noise test: add simulated flipping at the observed split-half disagreement rate and confirm conclusions survive.
design.multiplicity: Confirmatory set fixed in advance: three coverage roles (plus all-three combined) crossed with the three diagnostics, with Holm correction across them at a family-wise alpha of 0.05. One primary talent proxy is named in advance. Other proxies, playoff results and subgroup splits are labeled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Call the question supported only if all of the following hold on the development sample and the holdout: (1) within-team variance share of coverage exceeds the permutation null (lower 95% bound above the null mean) for at least the Shaper role and for combined coverage; (2) residual coverage variance after controlling for talent and counts is at least a preset fraction (for example 50%) of total, with a lower bound above that fraction; (3) the talent proxy has VIF below 5 against the counts, absolute correlation with coverage below a preset limit, the same sign across seasons, and does not absorb the role signal under the placebo roles. Call it rejected if the well-powered interval excludes the preset thresholds. Call it artifact if results vanish under the permutation or placebo tests or depend on near-threshold players. Otherwise report it as inconclusive or underpowered.
design.data_version: NBA per-game files and derived play-type possession records for 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs (420,993 possessions and 90 team-seasons as recorded), with the role-labeling rule and classifier version frozen and logged. 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) is the intended holdout, to be opened once after thresholds and code are frozen. Playoffs for 2025-26 (complete from 2026-06-21) are exploratory only. Record the as-of date 2026-07-13 and the file hashes.
